source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Enter BMC Web UI -> Click tab "Dashboard"
And also enter "Server Health" -> "Sensor Reading"

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: Sensor Reading & Threshold is human reable and match with spec.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sensor get 'PWR_STBY_HSC' 2>&1; echo ---SDR-FALLBACK---; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sdr elist 2>&1 | head -100
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: returns FULL raw `ipmitool (OOB lanplus) sensor get "<SENSOR>"` reading + threshold; user judges (read-only).

historical_reviews.deepseek: YES can retrieve a named sensor but supplies no authoritative meaning for STBY_HSC, standby rail boundary, required AC/DC/host/BMC state, units/scaling, state-dependent acceptance or proof that the UI and raw record are the same point. Its head-limited fallback is not complete evidence.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly treats the standby-domain definition and current power state as prerequisites and prohibits power/load changes. V3.1 additionally binds the reading to the exact HSC controller and always-on rail consumers, distinguishes it from HSC1-10, and requires state-conditioned zero/unavailable/threshold rules rather than one universal expected value.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 900/2291 accepts the generic sensor-get command without rail identity, power-state precondition, full SDR/UI correlation, specification value or protected credential handling.
historical_reviews.related_source_cases: Wistron-BMC-00085-V003 exposes a real conflict between this standby target and its copied GPU-stress procedure; that conflict belongs to the dynamic case and its stimulus must not be imported here. Wistron-BMC-00977-V002 separately checks IPMI list/field behavior. The preceding HSC1-10 family is a different set of switched power domains.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No sequence-1062 or Wistron-BMC-00191-V003 draft exists in the invalidated run; the invalid related record is the dynamic Wistron-BMC-00085-V003 variant.
historical_reviews.v3: No V3 record exists for this exact passive row. The V3.1 dynamic-row decision preserves the unresolved stimulus conflict but does not prevent a separately scoped passive standby telemetry check.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves PWR_STBY_HSC; ED-34 makes rail/controller/state/specification inputs Project readiness rather than permanent blockage; ED-35 forbids silently adding power transitions or GPU load; ED-38 requires preserved logs, no mutation/retry and engineer-owned verdict.

original_test_intent: Verify the single `PWR_STBY_HSC` telemetry point represents the Project-defined standby HSC power domain and is correctly shown in Dashboard and Server Health > Sensor Reading—with the proper controller/rail identity, quantity, units, status and supported thresholds—for the explicitly recorded system power state.
original_method: Establish the standby power topology and state matrix, identify the exact HSC controller channel and SDR/UI record, then passively capture nontruncated raw and UI values and compare them with state-specific Project limits. Preserve the current AC/DC, host and BMC state; do not use GPU stress or a power transition as part of this row.
manual_activity: The platform power owner identifies the standby HSC rail/controller, its always-on consumers and the state-specific acceptance matrix. An operator records the existing AC/DC/host/BMC condition without changing it. Automation may collect the named raw and UI telemetry; engineering decides whether that state-specific evidence satisfies the testcase.
required_inputs: Chassis/baseboard PN and revision, BMC/BIOS build and authoritative STBY_HSC definition
Standby power-tree boundary, upstream source, HSC controller designator/PN/revision and always-on downstream consumers
Required AC presence, host/DC state, BMC state, HSC enable state and any PSU redundancy prerequisites
Controller bus/address/channel/register, measured quantity, units, scaling, calibration and averaging window
Stable SDR/API/UI identity and state-specific normal range, tolerance, thresholds/hysteresis, status, zero/unavailable/stale behavior
Protected ipmitool/API/browser access and pinned reviewed `sensor.git` revision/checksum or approved manual collection
safety_requirements: Do not clear SEL, power, BMC or host logs; existing events establish whether standby power has been stable.

Do not change AC/DC or host power state merely to satisfy a missing state definition. Record the present state and stop if the required state is different until a separately approved transition plan exists.
Do not infer STBY_HSC is one of HSC1-10 or identify consumers from the label alone; use the Project power tree.
Do not apply GPU/module load from Wistron-BMC-00085-V003: its causal link to standby power is unproven and it is outside this Sensor Page scope.
Do not alter HSC enablement, thresholds, fan control, PSU feeds or firmware. A standby-domain disturbance can reset management or remove the recovery path.

Use secret-safe credentials, supported cipher negotiation and complete SDR/API output; do not expose `-P`, truncate to 100 lines, execute an unreviewed inaccessible Script or retry after stale/lost telemetry.
agent_execution_scope: Verify the standby-rail/controller map, currently applicable power-state row, stable sensor/UI identity, protected read client and governing specification before collection.

Capture PWR_STBY_HSC independently with controller source, quantity, units, value, threshold support/values, status, averaging window and timestamp; capture the exact unchanged Dashboard and Server Health presentation.
Record AC input, PSU redundancy, host/DC/BMC/HSC state and any known always-on consumers, then compare only with the approved rule for that state.
Preserve all evidence and make no log clear, load, AC/DC/host transition, controller/threshold/fan/firmware write, retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Define STBY_HSC, its exact rail/controller/consumer boundary and its separation from the ten numbered HSCs.
Approve the required power-state matrix and each state's range, tolerance, threshold/status/freshness and zero/unavailable behavior; approve the tool or override.
Determine whether the captured state is applicable and issue the formal verdict without treating an untested power state or the dynamic GPU-stress case as covered.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A direct exact-name read is a useful starting point, unlike the adjacent range cases, but it cannot establish rail semantics, applicable power state or UI/specification correctness. The fallback is incomplete, `-P` exposes credentials and cipher 17 may not be supported.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After resolving the standby controller/rail and current state, query the exact record through protected read-only access, retain its full SDR metadata and correlate its timestamped value and thresholds with the same UI point and state-specific specification.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The exact PWR_STBY_HSC name, Dashboard and Server Health paths, source Criteria, generic log-clear text, Script, DeepSeek proposal and 1/0-minute estimates remain preserved; Review does not edit Master or create a power transition.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a state-conditioned evidence row keyed by standby controller/rail plus AC/DC/host/BMC state; collect synchronized full SDR/API and UI data and compare it with the Project's calibrated rule for that exact state.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The Project's baseboard standby-power topology and BMC monitoring implementation.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record baseboard, PSU/HSC controller, BMC/SDR/WebUI, management client and Script revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform always-on/standby power tree, HSC telemetry/register definition, power-state specification, BMC SDR repository and WebUI schema.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds a verified rail/controller boundary and explicit state-dependent acceptance to the preserved passive UI inspection.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: One passive state does not validate S0/S5/G3 transitions, inrush, overload/trip, deassert/recovery, GPU-load coupling or the numbered HSC channels.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: STBY_HSC topology, applicable power state, state-specific acceptance, full read path and evidence contract.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A standby rail may remain energized with host DC off and may supply BMC/recovery functions; zero or unavailable can be correct or faulty depending on architecture and exact state.

project_override_considerations: A Project-approved Redfish/OEM or controller-vendor read may substitute for ipmitool only if the original method, replacement reason, engineer approval and equivalent controller/rail identity, value, units, thresholds, status, freshness and UI correlation are recorded. A reading from numbered HSCs, PSU output or host telemetry is not automatically equivalent.
expected_evidence: Chassis/baseboard/BMC identity and approved STBY_HSC controller/rail/upstream/consumer map
Recorded AC presence, PSU/feed redundancy, host/DC, BMC and HSC enable/fault state with applicable acceptance-matrix row
Full raw SDR/API identity, value, quantity/units, thresholds, status, calibration/window and synchronized timestamp plus redacted Dashboard and Server Health fields
State-specific vendor/Project comparison including zero/unavailable/stale interpretation and explicit untested-state coverage difference
Protected tool/Script provenance, preserved logs, no-load/no-power-transition/no-write/no-retry proof, final management health and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: This passive Sensor Page row consistently asks to display and compare PWR_STBY_HSC. It does not contain the GPU-stress mismatch present in the separate dynamic row. Undefined rail semantics and power state are readiness inputs, not an internal contradiction here.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The passive standby-power display objective is identifiable and can be executed after normal Project topology/state/specification inputs are supplied. Those missing inputs do not justify permanent BLOCKED or a guessed power transition.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Changes unconditional YES to PACKAGE and retains the useful exact-name read only after standby topology and state gating.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees with the hybrid result and adds the exact controller/always-on consumer boundary, separate HSC1-10 identity and a multi-state acceptance/coverage model.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces command-presence review with a power-state-conditioned raw/UI/specification correlation.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Keeps dynamic stimulus and IPMI list-format coverage distinct; neither substitutes for passive UI correctness in the recorded state.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: The invalid dynamic-row record informs the no-GPU-stress boundary only; this exact row has no invalid draft.

review_improvement: Prevents a valid-looking single sensor read in the wrong power state, or an unrelated GPU-load response, from being used as proof of standby HSC correctness, while avoiding an unnecessary permanent block.
independent_technical_reasoning: Standby power is architecture- and state-dependent: it can remain active while host main rails are off and may sustain the BMC or recovery logic. Therefore value, threshold and availability must be interpreted against the exact rail boundary and AC/DC/host/BMC state. Passive collection is safe after those inputs are known; changing state or load would add unapproved functional coverage and risk the management path.
